decision: Do not replace production classification yet. Continue boundary-preserving material inference and deterministic search-stability diagnostics.

editableFailures.reason: The converted cuts fail the editor’s crossing or minimum-spacing checks, including without simplification.
Family A has no cuts; a heart needs at least one per side.

limitations: All 32 photos were previously inspected; this is development evidence, not an untouched holdout.
Counts assess fitting to each method's own derived mask, not unknown original artwork or cutting paths.

Two of the six initial neutral-deviation gains are false reconstruction gains caused by wrong crops: basket and reflective building. Editor conversion rejects the latter; the former remains in the checked count.
The printed central flower is interpreted as a cut motif by all methods and passes all three; this is still a material-identity error.
Existing crop-support evidence was not reconstructed. The harness supported=0 values describe absent cached locator evidence, not 26 newly failed crop tests.
Ten seconds is the search allowance; final audits can exceed it. Reported wall times are single measurements, not a controlled speed benchmark.
No application code, model weights, crop proposal or acceptance limits changed.

findings.observation: The basket crop includes its contents and opening; the reflective building crop is an incorrect small section. Lobe sampling then learns from the wrong regions. An almost blank building mask has only 0.170625% class-one pixels, fits with zero cuts per sheet and passes engine self-mask checks, but fails the independent editor requirement of at least one cut per sheet.
findings.conclusion: A low self-mask error and valid cut geometry cannot establish correct crop or paper identification.

findings.observation: Exposed-lobe classification suppresses many stripes and floral ink marks. Similar-coloured printed papers, large same-colour ink regions and white paper with red text/dots remain ambiguous. The printed central flower survives every classifier as a false cut motif.
findings.conclusion: Lobe conditioning helps some printed papers but does not yet infer material identity reliably.

findings.observation: New masks round checks and narrow features that production preserves. The moon gains an extra cut, and thin details change in the hummingbird and dragonfly despite formal passes. Saved lobe scores are only 160 squared, upsampled to 320 before rectification; production classifies rectified source RGB.
findings.conclusion: Loss of boundary detail is observed. The share caused specifically by resampling versus classification needs a controlled native-resolution ablation.

findings.observation: RGB-only changes 0.966875% of observed production mask pixels but self-mask fit error rises from 1.958125% to 12.4725%; both select five cuts per sheet. Neutral deviation changes 1.545625% and yields 6.350625% fit error plus invalid geometry. Production still fails a feature check. Logs show different phase finalists, refinement reservation and early feature-recovery decisions.
findings.conclusion: The cut count alone does not explain this failure. Search sensitivity is implicated; no single causal branch is established without a counterfactual replay.

findings.observation: The mother/child motif, fox, petal flower and glare-affected tentacled motif gain editable checked candidates with neutralized query deviations. All original 13 production passes remain passes. The flower has an altered mask and residual false seams; these are promising candidates, not verified artwork recovery.
findings.conclusion: Keep these regressions and the failures together; do not select a per-photo method by its own fit error.

nextWork: Evaluate the fitted RGB classifier on native rectified pixels while holding cap samples, coefficients and crops fixed, to isolate resolution losses.
Test deterministic phase/finalist selection on the nativity and small mask perturbations; retain legal candidates and observed feature checks.
Train material embeddings with explicit lobe-to-overlap supervision and boundary preservation, rather than adding frozen foreground features.
Make future success summaries require editor-valid cuts and track empty-mask/crop failures separately; do not hide them by dropping cases.
